import json
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from app.exporter import export_csv

HEADER = "invoice_id,settlement_date,net_cents\n"

    row = dict(
        invoice_id="N-900",
        customer="NORTHSTAR",
        invoice_at="2026-09-10T12:00:00+00:00",
        settled_at="2026-09-15T16:00:00+00:00",
        status="PAID",
        gross_cents=1000,
        fee_cents=30,

        self.rows = load_sample()

        out = export_csv(self.rows, "NORTHSTAR", "2026-09")
        self.assertIn("N-102,", out)
        self.assertNotIn("N-101", out)

    def test_dst_offset_used_in_winter_months(self):
        # 2026-12-01T04:30Z is 2026-11-30 23:30 EST (UTC-5).
        row = ns_row(settled_at="2026-12-01T04:30:00+00:00")
        self.assertEqual(export_csv([row], "NORTHSTAR", "2026-11"), HEADER + "N-900,2026-11-30,970\n")
        self.assertEqual(export_csv([row], "NORTHSTAR", "2026-12"), HEADER)

    # R2
    def test_pending_with_null_settled_at_is_ignored_without_error(self):
        out = export_csv(self.rows, "NORTHSTAR", "2026-09")
        self.assertNotIn("N-104", out)

    def test_void_with_null_settled_at_is_ignored_without_error(self):
        row = ns_row(status="VOID", settled_at=None)
        self.assertEqual(export_csv([row], "NORTHSTAR", "2026-09"), HEADER)

    # R3
    def test_other_customers_excluded_from_northstar_export(self):
        self.assertNotIn("B-201", export_csv(self.rows, "NORTHSTAR", "2026-09"))

    def test_bluebird_keeps_invoice_export(self):
        self.assertEqual(export_csv(self.rows, "BLUEBIRD", "2026-09"), "invoice_id,amount_cents\nB-201,9000\n")

    # R4
    def test_header_columns_and_local_settlement_date(self):
        out = export_csv(self.rows, "NORTHSTAR", "2026-09")
        self.assertEqual(out.split("\n")[0], "invoice_id,settlement_date,net_cents")
        self.assertIn("N-102,2026-09-30,19400\n", out)
        self.assertNotIn("2026-10-01", out)

    def test_full_september_sample_output_sorted(self):
        self.assertEqual(

            HEADER + "N-103,2026-09-15,-5000\nN-102,2026-09-30,19400\n",
        )

        self.assertEqual(

            HEADER + "N-1,2026-09-15,970\nN-10,2026-09-15,970\nN-2,2026-09-15,970\n",
        )

        self.assertEqual(export_csv(self.rows, "NORTHSTAR", "2026-08"), "invoice_id,amount_cents\nN-101,10000\n")

    def test_paid_net_is_gross_minus_fee(self):
        self.assertIn("N-102,2026-09-30,19400\n", export_csv(self.rows, "NORTHSTAR", "2026-09"))

    def test_refund_net_is_negative_gross_fee_not_returned(self):
        out = export_csv(self.rows, "NORTHSTAR", "2026-09")
        self.assertIn("N-103,2026-09-15,-5000\n", out)

        for field in ("gross_cents", "fee_cents"):

                with self.subTest(field=field, value=bad):
                    with self.assertRaises(ValueError):

    def test_non_usd_row_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            export_csv([ns_row(currency="EUR")], "NORTHSTAR", "2026-09")

    def test_settled_at_without_offset_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):

        for status in ("PAID", "REFUNDED"):

        rows = self.rows + [ns_row(currency="EUR")]

            export_csv(rows, "NORTHSTAR", "2026-09")

    # R12
    def test_export_csv_signature_unchanged(self):
        self.assertEqual(list(inspect.signature(export_csv).parameters), ["rows", "customer", "month"])

    unittest.main()

findings.evidence: The period is chosen by plain string comparison. A malformed month such as "2026-9" counts as later than "2026-09" ('9' > '0'), so it goes to the settlement path and silently returns just the header: export_csv([PAID row settled 2026-09-15], "NORTHSTAR", "2026-9") -> 'invoice_id,settlement_date,net_cents\n'. The legacy invoice path also returns an empty result for malformed months, so this is not a regression. The engineer listed it as an assumption.

A PAID row with fee_cents greater than gross_cents is accepted and gives a negative net: gross 10, fee 50 -> 'X,2026-10-15,-40'. FIN-SETTLEMENT-2 only requires each value to be nonnegative and does not say whether fee > gross is valid.

Status matching is case-sensitive, and unknown or missing statuses are skipped without any error. A row with status 'paid' and a valid September settled_at is silently dropped: output is header only. This matches the rule as literally written, but upstream data in a different case would lose settled revenue without notice.

The tests cover the EDT case (sample) and an EST case (December). Nothing tests the DST changeover day itself or a 'Z' suffix. I checked these manually and they are correct: 2026-11-01T03:59Z -> 2026-10-31, 2026-11-01T04:30Z -> 2026-11-01, '2026-09-15T12:00:00Z' is accepted.

review.summary_for_business: NORTHSTAR now gets a settlement-based monthly export from September 2026. Each payment is placed in the month it settled in New York time, net of fees, and refunds deduct the full amount without returning the fee. These rules come from the approved Reporting Product (EXPORT-NS-1) and Finance Operations (FIN-SETTLEMENT-2) documents. The export stops with an error rather than guessing when data is bad: non-dollar currency, missing or ambiguous settlement times, or invalid amounts. Other customers, and NORTHSTAR months before September 2026, are unchanged. Two small questions are still open for Finance: whether a fee larger than the payment should be rejected, and whether status labels could ever arrive in a different letter case.

Amount and currency checks apply only to rows in the requested month. A bad settled_at on any PAID/REFUNDED NORTHSTAR row fails the whole export, whatever its month (documented by the engineer).
